title: Review of c06's pcell efficiency claim (SIDH): replicates on fresh seed 7 (mean yield 1.12-1.14 vs marker 0.94-0.99; deaths at yield percentile 0.045 vs marker 0.60), with large cells taking over the domain
summary: Ran world.py on seed 7 with labkit to t=100000 (200 frames at 500 steps) and with the author's genealogy.py to t=100000, then birthfate.py, deathsel.py and abslife.py. Cells form from the uniform particle soup by t~4500 and divide (genealogy: 15 persistent splits, generation 3, 0 merges, 51 deaths; labkit: 8 persistent splits, gen 2). Mean yield vs inert marker: 0.99/1.01 (t=13000), 1.07/1.02 (38000), 1.11/1.00 (63000), 1.13-1.14/0.97-0.99 (75500-88000), 1.12/0.94 (100000). Mature-cell deaths (23 with minlife 20) sit at yield percentile 0.045, all 23 below the median; marker 0.60 (10/23). Dying cells' birth rank 0.38 (marker 0.46); low-born vs high-born death share 0.75 vs 0.53 (marker 0.64 vs 0.62). Their own yield falls 0.98 -> 0.90 during life. Splits are unselected (0.55 vs 0.53). The particles sheet shows the population shifting from ~22 small cells to a few very large ones (labkit max/min area ratio 32) by t~60000.

verdicts.limitation: The birth-rank effect is modest here (0.38; low-born death share 0.75 vs 0.53 against a marker 0.64 vs 0.62), and dying cells lose 0.09 of yield in life, at the top of the claim's 0.03-0.08, so some within-life decline remains. The response coincides with the cells becoming few and large (sheet t=35000-100000), as the claim's limits say. I did not check the named track 53 on seed 0.
